result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers commit to (c), ground the choice in users building a real alert against live conditions, and name risks such as data dependency, drop-off and build cost, with ways to limit each. B covers more of the four named settings and adds a useful point about empty previews. A wins on item 5 because it says to reuse the carousel copy as helper text at each step, while B only keeps the carousel as a fallback to ship instead. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers commit to (c), argue well that building the alert against real conditions beats watching or reading, name risks with fixes, and propose cheap checks given the lack of data. B pulls ahead on rubric item 5: it says to reuse the carousel copy as helper text at each step, while A only keeps the carousel as a fallback and says nothing about what happens to the video or carousel material. B's point that an alert that never fires means it was set wrong is also a sharper success measure.
